title: Checkpoints & interrupted travel
label: CIVILIAN PROTECTION
deck: Avoid unnecessary travel through active fighting or uncertain checkpoints. Check the route and requirements as recently as possible, keep identification and essential medical information accessible, and avoid confrontation. A uniform, posted order or claimed safe corridor does not guarantee safe passage. Rules and protection risks differ by place.
tldr: Avoid unnecessary travel through active fighting or uncertain checkpoints. Check the route and requirements as recently as possible, keep identification and essential medical information accessible, and avoid confrontation. A uniform, posted order or claimed safe corridor does not guarantee safe passage. Rules and protection risks differ by place.
steps: Compare the danger of staying with the risks of the route. Do not travel only to investigate a closure. Have a known destination and another option.
Compare recent trusted local information with independently verified humanitarian information. Check dates and exact locations; old route advice may be unsafe.
Carry identification and medical information securely. Know where they are so you do not need a hurried search. Do not display sensitive details unnecessarily.
Remain calm, avoid sudden gestures and do not film an encounter when doing so increases danger. There is no universal script that guarantees safe treatment.
Have an agreed check-in and separation plan. Do not send a child or vulnerable person ahead alone to test a route.
next: Where you face detention or abuse risk, seek trusted local legal or humanitarian protection advice before travel when possible. Keep a private record of events only when doing so is safe.
watch: This is civilian safety planning, not advice to evade checkpoints or legal restrictions. Never assume passage based on a map, an insignia or an unverified promise.
without_help: If nobody can verify a route and travel is not immediately necessary, remain in the safer available place while reassessing. Do not assume a public convoy or unofficial driver has secured protection.
household: Assign a trusted adult to each person who needs assistance. Keep medicines, essential contacts and a workable reunion plan with the group. Make decisions around the least mobile person, not the fastest; avoid splitting the family without a clear, safe way to reconnect. For this situation, brief every person on the first action: decide whether travel is necessary. Agree who will manage children, pets or mobility needs while that action happens. This is civilian safety planning, not advice to evade checkpoints or legal restrictions. Never assume passage based on a map, an insignia or an unverified promise.
